candidate.answerReason: The only integer solution pairs are (6,3) and (12,3), giving exactly two solutions.

methods.label: Restrict the two factors
methods.explanation:
The left side is an integer, so \(y\) cannot be negative: then \(2^y\) would lie strictly between \(0\) and \(1\). Thus \(y\geq0\).

Since \(2^y>0\), the factors \(x-8\) and \(x-10\) are nonzero and have the same sign. Their absolute values differ by \(2\), and each must be a power of \(2\), including the possibility \(1=2^0\).

The smaller absolute value cannot be \(1\), because the larger would be \(3\). It cannot be at least \(4\), because both powers would then be divisible by \(4\), making their difference divisible by \(4\). Therefore the absolute values must be \(2\) and \(4\).

If the factors are positive, \(x-10=2\), giving \(x=12\). If they are negative, \(x-8=-2\), giving \(x=6\). In both cases the product is \(8=2^3\), so \(y=3\). These cases exhaust the possible factors and give two distinct pairs, \((6,3)\) and \((12,3)\). Thus there are \(2\) solutions, choice C.
